provisions.title: Standard of consent
provisions.text: (1) The consent given by the Data Principal shall be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous with a clear affirmative action, and shall signify an agreement to the processing of her personal data for the specified purpose and be limited to such personal data as is necessary for such specified purpose.

provisions.title: Exposure of Sensitive Information Due to Incompatible Policies
provisions.text: The product's intended functionality exposes information to certain actors in accordance with the developer's security policy, but this information is regarded as sensitive according to the intended security policies of other stakeholders.

examples.label: positive
negative

value.reason: The evidence shows `finale.resource` exposing the whole User model at `/api/Users` and `/api/Users/:id`. Only `password` and `totpSecret` are removed through `excludeAttributes`. Every other column is still serialised, including `email`, `username`, `role`, `lastLoginIp`, `profileImage`, `isActive` and a redacted field at models/user.ts:97 that may hold a token or secret. This is a deny-list rather than an allow-list, so any new or overlooked sensitive column gets exposed by default. The list endpoint has `pagination: false`, so a single request can return every user's personal data, including email, last login IP and role, which also shows who the admins are. This matches the positive example (returning the whole model) and not the negative one (an explicit attribute allow-list). It is a property-level authorization and data-minimisation failure. The evidence does not show any route-level auth middleware. Even if the endpoint requires login, any logged-in user could read every other user's data.
